headline: It turns out the advancements we’re getting in coding and computer use, combined with industry specific understand and general reasoning, can bring automation to a large number of areas of knowledge work. We’ll see it in animation, film production, gaming, manufacturing, architecture, product design, robotics, and more. All of these fields have the potential of driving far more output similar to what we’ve seen in software engineering. There’s no inherent finite demand for these categories of work. “Software is eating the world” is finally in a much bigger way happening because of AI.

headline: google-deepmind/mujoco
abstract: Multi-Joint dynamics with Contact. A general purpose physics simulator.https://mujoco.org MuJoCo stands for Multi-Joint dynamics with Contact. It is a general purpose physics engine that aims to facilitate research and development in robotics, biomechanics, graphics and animation, machine learning, and other areas which demand fast and accurate simulation of articulated structures interacting with their environment. This repository is maintained by Google DeepMind. MuJoCo has a C API and is intended for researchers and developers. The runtime simulation module is tuned to maximize performance and operates on low-level data structures that are preallocated by the built-in XML compiler. The library includes interactive visualization in native desktop windows and web browsers. MuJoCo further exposes a large number of utility functions for computing physics-related quantities. We also provide Python bindings and a plug-in for the Unity game engine. Documentation MuJoCo's documentation can be found at mujoco.readthedocs.io. Upcoming features due for the next release can be found in the changelog in the "latest" branch. Getting Started Try MuJoCo in your browser. Visit mujoco.org to explore MuJoCo on desktop or mobile with nothing to install, or open live.mujoco.org to inspect and drag and drop your own models in the WebAssembly version of the MuJoCo Studio app...
